opening.text: 凧あげの間違い探し、全5問。

unchiku.text: ここでひと休み。こよみ先生の季節のお話です。
凧のむかしの名前、知っていますか？
「いかのぼり」と呼ばれ、イカに似ているから、という説があります。
高く上がる凧は、見上げるだけで楽しいですね。

ending.text: これで5問目まで、おしまいです。
15個の違い、いくつ見つかりましたか。結果発表です。
チャンネル登録とベルで、毎朝8時半に問題が届きます。毎日の頭の体操にどうぞ。
ほかにも、いろいろな間違い探しがあります。もっと難しい問題に挑戦したい方は、画面の動画をクリックしてくださいね。

extra.text: 見つかった数を、あとでコメントで教えてくださいね。

images.style: A Japanese picture-book illustration in watercolor, but with BOLD, THICK, DARK ink outlines around every object (like a clear picture book for seniors), and CLEAR, SATURATED colors (not pale). Bright, clean background. Natural, hand-drawn, slightly rounded shapes; not geometric, not flat vector, not photorealistic. CLOSE-UP composition (not a wide landscape): the scene is seen from close, filling the picture. PORTRAIT-ISH composition, about 8:9. The painting fills the entire canvas edge to edge: no white border. No people. Absolutely no text, letters, numbers, logos or symbols anywhere. The MAIN SUBJECT named in the scene is drawn LARGE in the center of the picture. Around it, only a few other objects, each clearly separated with space around it, fully visible.
images.keep_alt: Keep everything else in the picture exactly the same: same composition, same position of every object, same colors, same style. Do not add or remove anything else. Leave no faint outline, ghost or smudge. No text.
images.keep_remove: Where an object is removed, fill the area naturally with what would be behind it, and leave no faint outline, ghost or smudge of the removed object.

questions.prompt: Scene: close-up of a winter riverbank (kawara) on a bright calm winter day: dry golden grass with a little frost, a wide gently flowing river with small grey pebbles on the near shore, bare willow trees and dry reeds in the background, clear pale blue sky. CENTER, LARGE (main subject): a big diamond-shaped paper kite, plain cream and blue with a simple geometric pattern and a long tail of paper bows, lying FLAT on the dry grass, its long string tied to a thick wooden stake hammered into the ground beside it. Winter only, with frost and bare trees: no Christmas, New Year's Eve or New Year decorations (no kagami-mochi, no shimenawa, no kadomatsu), no yuzu, no summer items, no snowman. Any kite is always lying FLAT on the ground or leaning on the ground, tied by its string to a wooden stake in the ground: no kite in the air, nothing hanging in the sky, the sky is clear and empty. Spread the listed objects over the whole picture at the given positions, far apart, never clustered. Keep every listed object BELOW the top fifth and ABOVE the bottom fifth of the picture. Each listed object is fully visible and rests on the ground, a flat stone or the grass; nothing floats. Each listed object is about one sixteenth of the picture width, VERY SMALL, with plenty of empty space around it. No letters, labels, numbers or writing anywhere (kites, bags and tins are plain, with simple geometric patterns only). No people, no hands. Do not use much red or orange: keep the light natural bright daylight-white and the whites ordinary white. Objects: (upper left, on the grass) a small blue thermos flask standing upright; (upper right, on the grass) a small stack of three grey stones; (middle left, on the grass) a small wicker picnic basket; (middle right, on a flat stone) a small wooden string reel with white string wound on it; (lower left, on a flat stone) a pair of small cream-colored knitted gloves; (lower right, on the grass) a small wooden stake with a short rope tied around it.
